free_tier.stated: Storage and egress are whatever your VPS/host allows. No provider quota exists. The cost moves to the host's bandwidth allowance.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Host bandwidth is paid directly to the server provider. IPFS documentation recommends fronting gateways with caching CDNs using standard Cache-Control, ETag, and X-Ipfs-Roots headers to minimize origin bandwidth consumption.

tooling: Kubo (go-ipfs), Rainbow (github.com/ipfs/rainbow), Someguy for delegated routing, Helia in-browser; rclone can talk to the Kubo RPC API via a webdav/MFS shim but there is no first-class rclone backend.
chaining: Does not multiply free storage. It only re-serves content you already paid to pin. Combined with a free pinning service it can turn 5 GB of free pinning into unmetered-looking reads, but only for 5 GB of content.
limits_note: Bandwidth of the VPS; DHT lookup latency on cold CIDs; no excess-use protection by default ('Unlike ipfs.io, a self-hosted gateway has no abuse protection by default').

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Self-hosting shifts network bandwidth accounting to the underlying hosting provider or CDN without eliminating upstream transit metering.

extras.egress_verbatim: You pay the host. IPFS docs recommend putting a CDN like Cloudflare in front of the gateway and setting Cache-Control/ETag/X-Ipfs-Roots for cacheability — which is the one genuinely correct architectural move in this slot, but it is Cloudflare's free egress you are relying on, not IPFS's.

extras.agent_focus: Decentralised storage / IPFS pinning judged on gateway egress economics: Pinata, Storacha/web3.storage, Filebase, 4EVERLAND, Lighthouse, thirdweb, Fleek, QuickNode, Infura, Kubo+self-host, dweb.link/ipfs.io, Sia/Skynet, Storj, Akash, Arweave (ar.io/Turbo/Irys), Walrus, Filecoin/Fil+/FCSS, BitTorrent, ZeroNet, Hypercore, Earthstar, Crust

binding_note: one stream is shaped, and aggregate throughput is the shaped rate times the number of streams
